requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion

rationale:
## Obligations and coverage

The obligations of `requirements.authoring.invocation` are satisfied:

1. **Author evidence for one existing requirement; author evidence for one existing named example; use the current project.** `src/main.rs#enum[Command]` accepts the single subject, configuration selection, output and verbosity options, and retains the alias. `src/main.rs#fn[main]` obtains the project root and dispatches the single-subject assessment. `src/setup.rs#fn[project_root]` starts from the current directory. `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[AuthoringSubject]/fn[sources]` routes definitions to `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]`, which looks up the exact name and rejects missing definitions and vocabulary terms. `configured_record` and `configured_assessment` perform the assessment and produce its evidence. The marked tests `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` verify successful assessment and unknown-subject rejection. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` exercises requirement and example records and single-subject selection of both. Its fixture defines both kinds. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` also exercises invocation from a nested project directory.

2. **Apply `requirements.authoring.refresh` to this command.** `src/main.rs#enum[Command]` declares the conflicting refresh flags. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_options]` applies the default missing-only behavior, makes stdout force assessment, and checks `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[subject_is_current]` before configuration resolution. `src/main.rs#fn[main]` reports a skipped current subject. The marked refresh/invocation test `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` verifies default and explicit missing selection, preservation without usable configuration or model calls, conflicting flags, explicit force, and stdout-implied force. This checks application of the cited refresh requirement rather than independently reassessing that requirement.

3. **Report the selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on completion** (five separate metadata obligations). `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]` constructs these outcome fields, and `src/main.rs#fn[main]` formats them into the completion report. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts the default report's subject/backend/model and Evidence/Usage metadata. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` verifies the corresponding stderr report and that its reported usage path exists. The marked verbose single-subject test also checks completion metadata remains available with verbosity enabled.

4. **Identify the evidence-file path by default; identify stdout when requested.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[AuthoringSubject]/fn[evidence_path]` computes the definition's evidence path. `configured_assessment` writes that file or stdout and returns the matching destination; `src/main.rs#fn[main]` reports the path or `Evidence: stdout`. The default CLI test checks the reported path resolves to the actual evidence file. The stdout test checks the stdout destination label and parses stdout as the evidence record.

5. **Send the completion report to stderr in stdout mode; send diagnostics to stderr in stdout mode.** `src/main.rs#fn[main]` uses `eprintln!` for stdout-mode metadata, false outcomes and verbose false rationales. Its reachable `src/main.rs#fn[print_coverage_warnings]` also writes diagnostics to stderr. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` covers true, false and FIXME judgments, with default and verbose reporting, asserting JSON-only stdout and the expected stderr metadata and diagnostics.

6. **Retain `author-evidence` as the single-subject alias.** The alias is declared in `src/main.rs#enum[Command]`. Both the default assessment test and stdout assessment test invoke it successfully; the refresh test also invokes it for a current named example.

All implementation paths identified above are marked roots or reachable from them. The additional judgment/rationale reporting in `main` is specified by the same item's `requirements.authoring.reporting` reference, whose text was reviewed. No unacknowledged gap was found.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
:::{req} reporting
By default, authoring MUST suppress per-subject `true` judgment lines and show
each `false` judgment's subject and outcome on stderr, on both terminals and
redirected output. Existing progress counters and completion summaries MUST remain
available; FIXME notices and authoring errors MUST remain visible. Single-subject
authoring MUST retain its subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and
usage-record metadata.
`-v` and `--verbose` MUST additionally show each false judgment's recorded Markdown
rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded
input snapshots. Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result,
without additional inference. In `--stdout` mode, stdout MUST remain only the
evidence JSON; verbose rationale and other diagnostics MUST go to stderr.
Verbosity MUST NOT change persistence, validation, or exit-status rules.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.invocation` {cite}`requirements.authoring.batch`
